body:
CURRENT REMOTE RUNNER AGREEMENT — Engram and TermAl. This is operating guidance; it grants no new execution, Git, installation or restart authority. Rev 27, 2026-11-21 (Engram::Fable): removes the agent SSH fallback under Greg's ban (rules-greg-no-agent-ssh-2026-11-21); the Mac was in federation the whole time. Rev 26 reconciled Windows B with rules-greg-windows-b-off-2026-11-14. Superseded assumptions and incident history remain in prior revisions and work notes.

ROUTE
Use the existing authenticated federation/native mailbox to hand a job to an appropriate native root on the runner host. That root uses its own local TermAl test-runs/launcher and returns terminal metadata and completion. Agents submit the exact input (a git bundle of the exact candidate commit, whose prerequisite is a commit the runner holds, or a pushed test/author-test ref) and read bounded summaries or the failure diagnostics they need. TermAl owns process, logs and wakes. No stdout following, polling or second transport.
A candidate's final FULL may run from such a bundle on a clean checkout; no test-ref push is needed. The test-ref route stays available when a pushed ref is wanted.
A directory entry alone does not prove a runnable session, and null telemetry does not prove route failure. A send receipt is fixed AT SEND TIME: durableButNotWoken means the wake was unconfirmed at that moment. Do not resend based on a receipt alone; use the exact-message current read.
NO AGENT SSH (Greg, 2026-11-21): no agent runs ssh, scp or any other side-channel remote shell or file copy to another host, not even as a fallback. Work on another host goes only through that host's TermAl remote session (federation, relay mail) or Git branches on origin. A missing or broken step goes to the federation owner (TermAl) or to Greg, never around it. TermAl's own federation transport is not an agent action and is unchanged.

HOSTS AND CAPACITY
ENGRAM NATIVE ROOTS:
- DL560: host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-4, the "DL560 · Engram runner" project, /home/greg/github/Engram-runner. Deliberately not connected to an Engram store; writes via domain mailbox 4369f879.
- Windows B is out of the Engram fleet; do not route tests or installs there.
- Mac Codex: host:abf8bda6-1ac7-485c-91ce-5a06ac453653::session-6201, /Users/greg/GitHub/Personal/Engram-runner. The Mac is in federation; reach it only through this route.
DL560 session-1 "Codex Live" belongs to the TermAl project. Engram registrations there were refused with 400, so it is NOT an Engram lane.
DL560 (144 cores; Greg, 2026-11-03: „DL560 ma wystarczająco mocy. 144 cores.”). Launch census, otherwise queue with the reason:
- MemAvailable ≥ 64 GiB;
- disk ≥ 60 GB plus the measured footprint (a FULL is about 13 GB);
- load < 110 (rules-remote-test-runs uses < 64 as Engram's own limit);
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=48 per job, with its own worktree and target, and no retry.
Every DL560 FULL needs Opus2's named GO: ONE shared FULL queue for both projects.
ALLOCATION (corrected 2026-11-06): Engram jobs, FULL and focused, go ONLY to session-4. TermAl uses session-3 and session-6.
Other hosts: Mac takes 1 job. Central runs 1 Cargo job, with slots through Opus2. Windows-only checks use Central under those slot rules.
WINDOWS B OFF (Greg, 2026-11-14; full words in rules-greg-windows-b-off-2026-11-14). Plan tests, gates and installs on Central, DL560 and Mac only. A case that truly needs Windows B with no alternative goes to Greg with its reason.

ISOLATION AND INPUT
Each project/host has a separate runner clone with the push URL disabled, and each job a fresh detached worktree with its own target and throwaway home under the ignored target. No shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, real ENGRAM_HOME or live store. A filtered test must actually execute at least one named test. A landing gate counts only under current AGENTS. An ordinary focused remote result is evidence, not a full gate. Every lane removes its worktrees, builds and temporary files once they have served (rules-greg-clean-up-after-work-2026-11-04).
FULL DURATION: a FULL runs detached (`--detach --notify`), or as a harness background task with an explicit timeout up to 7200000 ms; never at the harness's 30-minute default. Requesters say which in the request.
A queue REORDER only changes which request starts next (a marker); it never stops a queued or running waiter or wrapper.
Source-owner binaries and pins per lane: memory rules-remote-test-runs-2026-10-31, item 4.
